pr_comments: One slight concern I have with this change is the amount of polling that will be generated on these devices. With this PR there are three entities for each WeMo Insight device. We've had issues in the past (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/45904) where frequent polling will cause the device to drop from the network. Most of these devices will support device push messages, so polling will be disabled (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/46806). But if there are any helpers in Home Assistant that can merge the polling updates for entities on the same device, I'd be happy to use them here.

You could look into using the DataUpdateCoordinator, it allows you to handle the data collection centrally:

<https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data/#coordinated-single-api-poll-for-data-for-all-entities>

Thanks for the tip @frenck; I took a look at DataUpdateCoordinator. The WeMo component overrides some of the same methods, particularly [`should_poll`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c18b626d67fe07d532484dc82f03b063ac399868/homeassistant/components/wemo/entity.py#L147). I wasn't able to find a good way to keep this implementation and still use DataUpdateCoordinator. :(

Instead, I added a util.Throttle for the two sensors. So at least they don't cause 2x the requests.

@esev you can use a DateUpdateCoordinator and not use the entity. Also, `should_poll` should be set to False, because the data update coordinator has it's own update interval, which will then push the data to all 3 entities.

For now throttle will works, thanks for picking this up!

Here is a quick sketch on how a data update coordinator would work for Wemo.

![BF6A37CD-F52B-40E4-A4CF-86A492442957](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1444314/127019297-27e7975f-4d33-442b-82e7-bc10642b64e0.png)

Thanks @balloob! Is there a way to turn off the DateUpdateCoordinator's polling when the local push is working? We were finding in #45904 that the polling can cause issues. Local polling is mainly used as a backup now, when the device is on a different subnet and the local push subscription doesn't work.

It already works like that :) Every time you set data on a data update coordinator it will reset the update interval. That way it is always used as a backup. 

Shelly uses the timed interval to always raise UpdateFailed to mark the device as unavailable in case a local notification hasn't come in in time. It doesn't even try to poll.

issue_context.title: Extract wemo switch energy attributes into sensors
issue_context.body:
This issue is for the switch platform of the wemo integration.

The switch integration has embedded sensors for energy usage. This is no longer the preferred approach. Integrations using this approach should turn this data into standalone sensors.

This is important because Home Assistant is going to introduce home energy management (HEM) in 2021.8. HEM will be able to consume the data if it is exposed as standalone sensors.

To make sure that the sensors that represent total kWh is usable for HEM, set `state_class` to `measurement` and set `last_reset` to the timestamp of when the meter got reset (midnight if daily etc). [See sensor documentation for more information.](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor)

[Link to the architecture discussion.](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/discussions/579)

You don't have to remove them just yet, we might warn/remove them in the future globally. First step is to just get the other entities created.
